Biased Random Walk Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch55.R
centrality_biased_random_walk.Rd

Biased random walk centrality (Takes and Kosters 2011) is the share of time a random walker spends at a node when it prefers neighbors that have many ties and whose own neighbors are not tied to each other. From node \(v\) the walker moves to the neighbor \(w\) with probability proportional to \(\alpha f_{deg}(w) + (1 - \alpha) f_{nd}(w)\), where $$f_{deg}(v) = 1 - \frac{1}{|N(v)|}, \qquad f_{nd}(v) = 1 - \sum_{w \in N(v)} \frac{|N(w) \cap N(v)|}{(|N(w)| - 1)\,|N(v)|},$$ and with probability \(p\) it jumps to a node chosen uniformly.

Usage

centrality_biased_random_walk(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses brw_alpha (the weight of the degree term, default 0.5) and brw_jump (the jump probability, default 0.15).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order, summing to one.

Details

The source estimates the share of visits with one walk of ten steps per node from a random start, so its result varies from run to run. The value returned here is the stationary distribution of the same walk, the limit of that share, and needs no random numbers. The scores sum to one.

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. brw_alpha is 0.5 and brw_jump is 0.15 by default, the values of the source. The source leaves three cases open. A neighbor of degree one adds nothing to \(f_{nd}\). When every neighbor of a node has weight zero the walker picks among them uniformly. From an isolated node the walker always jumps. A brw_alpha outside \([0,1]\) or a brw_jump outside \((0,1]\) raises a cograph_bad_parameter error.

References

Takes, F. W. and Kosters, W. A. (2011). Identifying prominent actors in online social networks using biased random walks. In Proceedings of the 23rd Benelux Conference on Artificial Intelligence (BNAIC 2011), 215-222.

See also

centrality_pagerank, centrality.

Examples

centrality_biased_random_walk(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.09562519 0.10717857 0.10851157 0.11682470 0.10427429 0.10025709 0.08266489 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.09577127 0.10051426 0.08837818
